clue.text: News reader?

parts.note: the four letters of 'News' are the cardinal points North, East, West, South, which this instrument reads off its dial

explanation.surface: A question about who presents the evening bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News reader' looks like a broadcaster; split it as N, E, W, S, the points a navigator's dial shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational instrument with a magnetised needle shows north, east, west and south, so it literally reads N-E-W-S.

clue.text: Storm protection

definitions.meaning: to storm a position is to rush at it in attack
having someone in your care, as in a child left in your keeping

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an attacking rush at the enemy, and custody or care, as in 'in my charge'.

clue.text: Hawk lifts royal sheep above the tops of elm trees

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits above the next
in a down clue, lifting the words royal sheep raises them so they read upwards

parts.note: K is King, a royal
a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: the first letters of the words elm and trees

explanation.surface: A bird of prey carries off a sheep from a royal flock and soars over the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' pretends to be the bird but is the verb meaning sell. 'lifts' turns K + RAM upwards into MARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to peddle or sell them, which is what you do when you put something on sale.

clue.text: Supplements that might cause grumbling?

definitions.meaning: additional sections at the back of a book
a 'grumbling' appendix is the medical name for one giving mild, recurring pain; the plural organs might all grumble

explanation.definitionFit: Supplements added at the end of a book are its extra sections, and the bodily organ of the same name is known for grumbling.

clue.text: Great manager

definitions.meaning: an informal word of approval, excellent
short for superintendent, the person who runs a building or a police division

explanation.definitionFit: Informally it means excellent, and as a clipped noun it is the superintendent who looks after a building.

clue.text: Bean you are told to put in liqueur

indicators.note: these words say one piece is inserted into the bean

parts.note: the cacao bean is the source of chocolate

indicators.note: told signals the words you are are heard spoken, as in text-speak

parts.note: spoken, this sounds like the two letters U and R

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop a coffee or cocoa bean into a glass of liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' is the sound signal: 'you are' heard aloud is text-speak's two letters, set after the bean's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an orange-flavoured spirit named after a Caribbean island, often coloured blue.

clue.text: Fabulous creature presses on each star thistle, for example

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits pressing down on the next

parts.note: the centaur of Greek myth is half man, half horse

explanation.surface: A mythical beast tramples each thistle in its path.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the botanical genus of knapweeds and cornflowers, of which the star thistle is one member.

clue.text: Schedule time and relaxation — otherwise heads roll!

indicators.note: rolling the letters moves the front pair round to the back
the first letters of the words time, and, relaxation, otherwise

explanation.surface: A boss warns that the duty roster must include time off, or there will be sackings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' gives TARO; 'roll' carries TA round to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of who does which duty and when is a schedule of turns.

clue.text: Correct a chess move — take it back!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, that is hold, the next piece
a move signals the letters of a chess are rearranged
back means it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A chess player admits a bad move and asks to retract it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges the letters into CHASSE, itself a dance step; 'take' has it hold 'it' turned 'back'. 'Correct' is the old sense of punish.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a child in the old sense is to punish or reprimand them severely.

clue.text: Ruler's sexy lover gets gold and diamonds

indicators.note: sexy is used loosely as a sign the word lover is stirred up into new order

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
D is the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A monarch's attractive paramour is showered with gold and jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sexy' rearranges LOVER into OVERL.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme lord who holds power over other lords is a ruler of the highest rank.

clue.text: Anchor just lifted, ready for a journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A sailor reports the anchor raised and the ship set to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for an anchor that has just broken clear of the seabed as it is weighed.

clue.text: Bore to babble about English goal

indicators.note: about means the babbling word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on foolishly
the net is the goal in football

explanation.surface: Talking at length about an English goal makes one a crashing bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the verb meaning drill into.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore through something is to drill or pierce your way into it.

clue.text: Golf range played over par? Not by him!

definitions.text: Golf range played over par? Not by him!

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters lie across the piece for par

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: played signals golf and range are worked into a new order

parts.note: par is the norm, the standard

explanation.surface: At the driving range, playing over par is something this champion never did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' gives GREGAN, which 'over' wraps round the standard. Greg Norman is the Australian golfer long ranked world number one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian golf champion, nicknamed the Great White Shark, who was rarely over par on a course.

clue.text: Language of email service without vowels

indicators.note: without the vowels says the vowel letters are removed from the email service

parts.note: Hotmail is the well-known webmail provider

explanation.surface: A grumble about the language used by a webmail company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without vowels' drops O, A and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The markup language that structures web pages is a computer language, not a spoken one.

clue.text: Vegetable, green and sweet

parts.note: a pepper is a vegetable
mint is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A shopping list: a vegetable, something green, and a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured confection is a sweet, a British word for a piece of candy.

clue.text: Negotiator: I translate secrets into Norwegian

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the abbreviation for Norwegian

parts.note: Nor is the abbreviation for Norwegian

indicators.note: translate means the letters of secrets are put into new form

explanation.surface: A go-between confesses to rendering confidential documents into Norwegian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translate' gives TERCESS, which 'into' places inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pleads or mediates on another's behalf acts as a go-between.

clue.text: A cucubebe?

parts.note: the invented word has 'cube' set inside 'cube', just as the four-dimensional figure is drawn as one cube inside another

explanation.surface: A puzzling made-up word, like a typo or a nonsense name.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-dimensional hypercube is usually pictured as a small cube nested inside a larger one.

clue.text: This can shoot down Spooner's top boast

indicators.note: a Spoonerism swaps the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: the boss is the top person
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: Something capable of bringing down a bragging chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping B and CR of BOSS CROW gives CROSS BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical bow firing bolts is a weapon that can bring down a target.

clue.text: It's more ridiculous — I'm lost for words after Australian has bowled Root

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sound at the end

parts.note: b is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled
a surd is an irrational root in mathematics
er is the sound of someone groping for words

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator is speechless when an Australian bowls out Joe Root, England's batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an English cricketer, but here 'Root' is the mathematical surd.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of absurd is a word for something even sillier or more ludicrous.

clue.text: Tramp's uberpuzzle — over a billion approve

indicators.note: over means the muddled letters go across, around, the letter for a billion
puzzle signals the letters of Tramp's and uber are muddled

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A vagrant's super-puzzle earns approval from over a billion people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uberpuzzle' is one printed word split in two: its tail 'puzzle' mixes the letters before it, and 'over' wraps the result round the billion.
explanation.definitionFit: To give official approval without scrutiny is to authorise something mechanically, like stamping a document.

clue.text: Plot flirts with danger

indicators.note: flirts suggests the letters of danger dance about loosely

explanation.surface: Someone who toys with danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme; it is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land, such as an allotment, is a patch that can be cultivated.

clue.text: A vehicle with 50% engine capacity lacks motor co-ordination

definitions.note: verb phrase standing for an adjective: 'is unable to coordinate movement'

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle

indicators.note: fifty per cent keeps just half of the engine measure

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, measures engine capacity

explanation.surface: A car running at half power that cannot drive properly.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' keeps one C of CC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is a medical loss of control over bodily movements, describing someone unable to coordinate muscles.

clue.text: Told small joke

parts.note: a pun is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a brief gag.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spun a yarn is to have told a story.

clue.text: Dog sprinted after socialist's bone for fruit

indicators.note: after puts the dog and running pieces behind the socialist

parts.note: a red is a socialist
a cur is a mongrel dog
ran means sprinted
T, as in a T-bone steak

explanation.surface: A dog dashes after a socialist's bone in search of food.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the shape of the bone in a T-bone steak.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red berry grown on bushes is a soft fruit.

clue.text: Trainee pet bites revolting little man

indicators.note: bites means the pet holds the other piece in its jaws

parts.note: a cat is a pet

indicators.note: revolting means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the man's name Edward

explanation.surface: A trainee's pet sinks its teeth into a nasty small fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A student at a military or police academy is a trainee officer.

clue.text: Fit in baguette?

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie inside the word baguette

explanation.surface: Asks whether something fits inside a loaf of French bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' seems to mean go inside; it is a bout of shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of fever with shivering, as in malaria, is a fit.

clue.text: "Defender's daughter kidnapped by young man" — by this paper (not the Scotsman)

indicators.note: kidnapped by means the daughter is held inside the young man

parts.note: a boy is a young man

indicators.note: not means the Scotsman is taken away from this paper

parts.note: the clue appears in the Guardian newspaper
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style headline about a kidnapping, with a jab at a rival Scottish newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotsman' looks like the Edinburgh newspaper but is IAN; GUARDIAN minus IAN leaves GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal protector who shields someone from harm is a defender.

clue.text: Hiding behind executive table

indicators.note: hiding means the letters are tucked away within behind executive

explanation.surface: A boss cowering behind a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding behind' reads as one phrase, but 'behind' is part of the text that holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabetical list, or a table of figures such as a price measure, is an index.

clue.text: With stream flowing, it's most relaxing

indicators.note: flowing signals the letters of stream run into a new order

explanation.surface: Sitting by a babbling brook is the most soothing thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges STREAM into ARMEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth suggests cosiness and comfort, so the most cosy place is the most relaxing.

clue.text: Turn? I can't — it's enormous!

indicators.note: turn signals the letters of I can't and it are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver complains that a huge vehicle cannot make a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the ship that could not turn in time to avoid the iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Titans of Greek myth, the word describes something of gigantic size.
